nodes.title: Algebraic equivalence over the ground field
nodes.statement: For a finite-type separated k-scheme X, let Alg_i(X/k) be the subgroup of the integral Chow group CH_i(X) generated by differences t₁!Z − t₀!Z, where T is a smooth geometrically integral quasi-projective k-scheme of dimension e, t₀,t₁ are k-points, Z lies in CH_{i+e}(T×X), and t! denotes refined Gysin for the fibre inclusion. Two integral cycles are algebraically equivalent over k when their Chow-class difference lies in this subgroup. For smooth pure-dimensional X and a characteristic-zero coefficient field F, let I_alg^j(X;F) be the F-span of the image of Alg_{dim X−j}(X/k) in CH^j(X)⊗F, and put A_alg^j(X;F)=(CH^j(X)⊗F)/I_alg^j. Disconnected X is treated componentwise.
hypotheses: k is any field for the definition; X is separated of finite type.
The parameter is connected through geometric integrality and has two ground-field rational points; geometric algebraic equivalence after base change is a different relation.
Integral CH_i, refined fibre Gysin and scalar extension are imported, not encoded using raw cycle equality.
proofSteps: Use the SF.5 Chow carrier and fibre Gysin along the regular immersions supplied by smoothness of T.
Take the subgroup generated by these differences; exchanging the two points gives negatives. Products of parameter spaces combine sums.

Use ACMV Proposition 2.10 to compare with the smooth-integral-parameter definition without a quasi-projectivity restriction. Extend coefficients by span, not by declaring torsion cycles nonzero rational classes.
acceptance: Membership is invariant under changing a representative by rational equivalence.
The relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive; it is not defined as equality of cycle classes in a selected cohomology theory.

sources.locator: Definition 2.1 and Remark 2.3, p. 4; Proposition 2.10, pp. 7–8; Proposition 2.5, p. 5

nodes.title: Algebraic equivalence is adequate
nodes.statement: For smooth projective k-schemes and characteristic-zero F, the family I_alg is an adequate relation in MC.0/adequate-equivalence-relation: it is graded, stable under all morphism pullbacks, proper pushforwards and multiplication by arbitrary Chow classes. The integral dimension-graded subgroup is also preserved by proper pushforward, flat pullback, refined Gysin and exterior product with an arbitrary class. Consequently composition, action, transpose and tensor of correspondences descend to the algebraic quotient.
hypotheses: Use algebraic equivalence over k as defined above, and the imported SF.5 operations.
A morphism between smooth projective schemes factors as its regular graph followed by a smooth projection, supplying the required lci pullback.
proofSteps: Commute fibre Gysin with proper pushforward, flat pullback and refined Gysin, using the respective SF.5 base-change/interchange identities. Each family difference remains a family difference.
Multiplication by a fixed class is diagonal Gysin applied to exterior product; carry the fixed class along T and apply the same compatibility.

Tensor with F and apply the existing adequate-relation quotient construction. For sums of families use products of geometrically integral parameters, not a disconnected parameter joining unrelated fibres.
acceptance: A relation that only permits proper pushforward, without pullback or multiplication, does not meet adequacy.
Every correspondence operation already imported descends with exactly the same degree convention.

nodes.title: Curve parameters for algebraic equivalence
nodes.statement: Over a perfect field k, a class in Alg_i(X/k) is a difference of refined fibres of one cycle on C×X for a smooth projective geometrically integral curve C/k and two k-points. Over an arbitrary field a smooth quasi-projective geometrically integral curve suffices. These descriptions agree with the smooth-parameter subgroup, and for a smooth projective geometrically integral X over an algebraically closed field, Alg_0(X/k)=ker(deg:CH_0(X)→ℤ).
hypotheses: X is separated and of finite type over k.
Projective smooth curve normal form is asserted integrally only when k is perfect; no such assertion is made over an imperfect field without the source’s p-power qualification.
proofSteps: Use the prescribed-point Bertini statement requested of SF.4 (ACMV Appendix A), not the weaker existing smoothness-only Bertini target.

Restrict the family to a smooth quasi-projective curve containing the marked points, as in Proposition 2.10; closure of its cycle and refined Gysin give the projective form over a perfect field (Lemma 2.8).

For zero-cycles use Lemma 2.9 and Proposition 2.11: degree-zero combinations on a smooth parameter are algebraically trivial; apply the diagonal family on smooth X to degree-zero zero-cycles as in Lemma 2.9. Retain smoothness and projectivity, the explicit Proposition 2.11 hypotheses.
acceptance: For P¹ a degree-zero class is zero already rationally, whereas a positive-genus curve has nonzero algebraically trivial classes.
The theorem retains the ground-field rational marked points; passing to an algebraic closure is not a descent proof.

sources.match: These give curve parameter spaces, the perfect-field projective form, and degree-zero zero-cycles. Only the projective integral zero-cycle case is consumed here.

nodes.title: Algebraic equivalence is homological for a selected Weil theory
nodes.statement: Let k be any field, F be a characteristic-zero coefficient field, and H be a selected classical Weil cohomology of the geometric base change, with F embedded in its coefficient field. Then I_alg^j(X;F) is contained in I_H^j(X;F) for every smooth projective X/k. Define I_H directly as the kernel of CH^j(X)⊗F → CH^j(X_k̄)⊗F → H^{2j}(X_k̄), using flat base change and the componentwise classical Weil cycle class. This agrees with the geometric relation named by MC.2/homological-equivalence and the class-map formula in MC.2/weil-cohomology-by-base-change; its later realization on motives is not consumed here. It depends on H; independence of H is not a theorem here.
hypotheses: The early MC.2 axioms include products, Poincaré duality, trace and cycle classes with the usual degree and Gysin compatibilities.
Classical Weil cohomology has characteristic-zero coefficients; integral arithmetic étale cohomology is outside this assertion.

For nonclosed k the cycle-class formula is defined directly by the existing flat field-extension maps, their filtered algebraic-extension limit, and the componentwise Weil theory. The full MC.2/weil-cohomology-by-base-change node also constructs motive realization and lists MC.1/motives-universal-property; importing that full construction before MC.0 would be circular. Only the displayed geometric formula is used here.
proofSteps: Base change an algebraic family to an algebraic closure; the subgroup base-change map preserves its class.
Use curve-parameterisation over the algebraically closed field and extend the cycle to a smooth projective curve parameter using localization.
The two rational point classes of that connected curve agree in H²(C)(1), since their traces are both one and top cohomology has dimension one.
Fibre cycle classes are obtained by the same pull-product-push formula from the parameter point class. Their difference therefore has cycle class zero. Extend linearly to F.
acceptance: The elliptic divisor [P]−[O] is killed by the geometric Weil cycle class even when its rational Chow class is nonzero.
No conclusion that an integral arithmetic class vanishes is extracted from this comparison.

sources.match: Supplies top-degree trace, Künneth and cycle-class pull-product-push compatibility. Together with curve parameterisation these prove the stated inclusion; this is a derivation from the axioms, not a separately quoted comparison theorem.

nodes.title: The comparison chain of cycle quotients
nodes.statement: For smooth projective X/k over any field k and a selected geometric classical Weil theory H, rational equivalence implies algebraic equivalence, which implies H-homological equivalence, which implies numerical equivalence. With F coefficients this gives surjective graded maps CH^*(X)⊗F → A_alg^*(X;F) → A_H^*(X;F) → A_num^*(X;F), and identity-on-objects F-linear tensor functors between the corresponding degree-zero correspondence categories. All maps respect composition, graphs, tensor, transpose and the actions for which the corresponding quotient is defined.
hypotheses: Use the already planned adequate-equivalence quotient construction and numerical relation.
Numerical equivalence tests the degree against every complementary-codimension class, componentwise; the zero relation is rational equivalence on the Chow carrier.
No reverse implication, independence of H or standard conjecture is asserted.
proofSteps: A rationally zero class is the zero element of CH and hence belongs to Alg. Compare with the rational-curve-fibre presentation of rational equivalence.

Use algebraic-implies-homological. For H⇒num use cycle-class multiplicativity and the trace-degree formula: a zero cycle class has zero degree pairing with every complementary class. This is already an API theorem of MC.2/homological-equivalence.
Apply quotient universal properties to inclusions of kernel families. Adequacy supplies well-defined composition and tensor on each quotient; quotient surjectivity on each Hom gives the functors.
acceptance: On P¹, degree distinguishes a point from zero in all four quotients.
On an elliptic curve over ℂ, an infinite-order degree-zero divisor is nonzero rationally and zero algebraically, so the first quotient map need not be injective.

The zero adequate family and the indiscrete family are distinct. Numerical equivalence is coarsest only among nontrivial adequate families (I⁰(Spec k)=0), as retained in the numerical-equivalence target.

sources.match: Provides rational/numerical quotient and cycle-class context, and identifies the reverse numerical-to-homological comparison as conjectural. The forward chain here is derived from the preceding algebraic comparison and the imported trace-degree API, rather than stated in this source.
Rational-curve triviality represents precisely the zero Chow class, so rational equivalence is contained in algebraic equivalence.

nodes.title: Universal support for zero-cycles

The support may depend on L. Separately, a fixed support Y⊂X is universally supporting if this same surjectivity holds for every field extension L/k with Y_L the base change of Y. Keep these two quantified statements distinct.
hypotheses: Properness makes the closed-immersion pushforward and degree available.
The zero-cycle Chow group and base change belong to SF.5. This is a property of existing schemes/Chow groups, not a replacement for those carriers.
proofSteps: State the algebraically closed extension quantifier before the existential support and use the actual SF.5 closed-immersion pushforward.
Package witnesses, dimension bounds and monotonicity; separate the stronger fixed-support condition needed by the elementary generic-point decomposition.

Prove stability under base-field extension by composing the field embeddings. Transport through a proper map when its base-changed CH_0 pushforward is surjective and the image of a support has the required dimension.

nodes.title: Support and decomposition of a multiple of the diagonal
nodes.statement: Let X/k be smooth projective geometrically integral of dimension d and Y⊂X a closed reduced support of dimension at most s. If CH_0(Y_Ω)→CH_0(X_Ω) is surjective for an algebraic closure Ω of k(X), then there are N>0, a proper closed D⊊X, and Γ_D,Γ_Y in integral CH_d(X×X), supported respectively on D×X and X×Y, such that N[Δ_X]=Γ_D+Γ_Y. If surjectivity already holds over k(X), N=1 is possible. The first factor is the generic-point factor. A characteristic-zero smooth proper version and the passage from varying algebraically closed supports to a usable decomposition are separately identified assembly obligations.
hypotheses: X is nonempty; d=0 is allowed and yields D empty.
The hypothesis specifies a fixed Y defined over k and its base change to Ω, rather than a support chosen only after an unrelated extension.
The smooth proper extension uses a smooth projective birational model and birational invariance of CH_0.
proofSteps: Restrict the diagonal along the generic point of the first factor. Its class is a zero-cycle on X_{k(X)}. Surjectivity gives a cycle from Y after passage to Ω.
Cycles, rational functions and their finite relations descend to a finite extension E/k(X). Apply the proper norm: restriction followed by norm is multiplication by [E:k(X)].
Spread the normed Y-cycle and the equality over a nonempty open U⊂X, using the direct-limit description of Chow groups at the generic point.
Localization for (X∖U)×X makes the remaining difference the pushforward of a class supported on D×X. Enlarging D is harmless. No injectivity at the left of the localization sequence is used.
acceptance: For P¹, Δ=[point×P¹]+[P¹×point], with N=1 and the indicated support orientation.
Surjectivity only over Ω permits a nonunit N; it does not give an integral universal degree isomorphism.
For a positive-genus complex curve, zero-dimensional support would force the identity on H¹ to factor through points and hence vanish, a contradiction.

nodes.title: Correspondences on cohomology sheaves
nodes.statement: For smooth projective pure-dimensional complex X,Y, a constant abelian coefficient group A and c∈CH^{dim X+r}(X×Y), construct c_*:H^p(X,ℋ_X^q(A))→H^{p+r}(Y,ℋ_Y^{q+r}(A(r))), where ℋ^q is the Zariski sheaf associated to U↦H^q(U(ℂ),A). The action is additive in c, annihilates algebraic equivalence, has the diagonal as identity, and respects composition with the displayed shifts. The real closed application uses the corresponding nonequivariant semialgebraic cohomology over C=R(i), with its supplier interface explicitly requested; ordinary Zariski cohomology of a constant sheaf is a different object.
hypotheses: The Bloch–Ogus/Gersten interface supplies cycle classes in bidegree (c,c), cup products, proper trace, flat pullback, residues and the projection and base-change formulas.
For negative sheaf-cohomology degrees the groups are zero. Twists in an iterated action are added.
Integral coefficients are retained for the action; rationalization is applied only in the vanishing theorem.
proofSteps: Use c’s Bloch–Ogus class on X×Y. Pull back α by the first projection, cup with that class and trace along the second projection. Codimension dim X+r and trace shift −dim X give the shift (r,r) and twist r.
Prove the formula on Gersten/Cousin representatives, checking residue compatibility and the push-pull square. Correct the ambient target of CTV Lemma 9.3 as recorded in E48.
Projection and base change on X×Y×Z identify the iterated action with composition. For c=Δ use the graph/projection identities.

For a family over a smooth connected curve, the two fibre restrictions have the same action; the Gersten/cycle-class argument of Proposition 9.1 kills their difference. Thus factor through the algebraic quotient, not merely the rational quotient.
acceptance: The action is a map of the actual Bloch–Ogus groups supplied by SF.2, not an arbitrary collection of linear maps called a realization.
All support-factorization formulas are checked with the forward p₂-push convention.

nodes.title: Vanishing from a supported diagonal
nodes.statement: Let X/ℂ be smooth projective connected of dimension d, with NΔ=Γ_D+Γ_Y as above, dim D≤d−1 and dim Y≤s. For every abelian group A and every p<d−s with p≥0, multiplication by N annihilates H^p(X,ℋ_X^d(A)). In particular H^p(X,ℋ_X^d(ℚ))=0 in that range. The same implication applies to the nonequivariant characteristic-zero semialgebraic cohomology-sheaf theory satisfying the explicitly requested Bloch–Ogus and support-factorization interface.
hypotheses: Use integral diagonal decomposition and the forward correspondence action.

Resolve the actual projected images of individual integral cycle components in characteristic zero; their dimensions satisfy the support bounds, and their strict transforms push forward with generic degree one.
The universal-support-to-decomposition adapter is not an extra unmentioned hypothesis: its verification is recorded as gap MC0-G1 for the real closed target.
proofSteps: Write each supported correspondence as a finite sum of integral cycle components. For a component take its actual image W in the supported factor, resolve W projectively, and close the inverse image over the birational isomorphism locus. The component dominates W, so its strict transform pushes forward to that component with degree one. This gives a finite sum of factorizations without changing N; clear denominators first only if starting from a rational decomposition.
For each D×X component with smooth model W̃ of its first-projection image, the action factors through H^p(W̃,ℋ_{W̃}^d(A)), which vanishes because dim W̃≤dim D<d.

For each X×Y component put w=dim W̃≤s for a smooth model of its second-projection image. Its action factors through H^{p−(d−w)}(W̃,ℋ_{W̃}^w(A(w−d))); the twist w−d agrees with the correspondence degree. This group vanishes because p−(d−w)<0 when p<d−s.
The diagonal action is the identity, so N kills the group. On ℚ-vector spaces N is invertible; this is the reason for rational vanishing.
acceptance: For surface support s=2 and d≥3, p=d−3 is strictly below d−2.
At p=d−s the second factor has degree zero and the argument supplies no vanishing.
Integral annihilation by N is never reported as integral vanishing.

nodes.title: Universal surface support over a real closed field
nodes.statement: Let R be real closed, C=R(i), and X/R smooth proper geometrically integral of dimension d≥3. Suppose UniversalCH0Support(X,2). Then H^{d−3}(X_C,ℋ_{X_C}^d(ℚ))=0 and H^{d−3}(X,ℋ_X^d(ℚ(d−1)))=0. Here the first sheaf is defined by nonequivariant semialgebraic cohomology of U(C), and the second by G-equivariant semialgebraic cohomology, G=Gal(C/R). These are the two rational vanishings in the proof of BW Proposition 5.2, not its further torsion/finite-dimensional conclusions.
hypotheses: The support hypothesis is integral and quantified over all algebraically closed extensions of R. No hypothesis X(R)=∅ is imposed.
The SF.2 real closed Bloch–Ogus interface, universal-support adapter and proper/projective adapter are explicitly requested or recorded as gaps.
The Tate twist ℚ(d−1) has the sign action (−1)^{d−1}; division by two is allowed.
proofSteps: Use universal support and the diagonal argument with s=2, p=d−3 to obtain the nonequivariant rational vanishing; the exact descent/spread step from varying supports remains MC0-G1.
Write π:X_C→X. BW Proposition 5.1(i) identifies ℋ_X^d(ℚ[G]) with π_*ℋ_{X_C}^d(ℚ), and its acyclicity gives the corresponding isomorphism on H^{d−3}.
Split the regular rational G-module by (1+σ)/2 and (1−σ)/2. The sign representation ℚ(d−1) is a direct summand, so its cohomology group is a direct summand of the zero group.
acceptance: For d=3 the first group is H⁰(ℋ³(ℚ)); p=d−3 is not substituted into the second sheaf degree.
Neither ℓ-adic replacement of the semialgebraic sheaf nor an integral splitting by 1/2 is accepted.
MC.7 imports these two vanishing statements; the integral Hodge assertions and BW Proposition 5.2’s remaining consequences are outside MC.0.

nodes.title: Zero-cycles on low-degree hypersurfaces
nodes.statement: Let K be algebraically closed of characteristic zero, n≥2, and X⊂Pⁿ_K a smooth geometrically integral hypersurface of degree e with 1≤e≤n. Then deg:CH_0(X)→ℤ is an isomorphism. In particular this remains true over every algebraically closed extension of K. This is the low-degree conclusion of Roitman’s Theorem 6(a), extended from that paper’s uncountable-field convention by the elementary proof below, with n the ambient projective dimension, not dim X.
hypotheses: Integral Chow groups are used; e may equal n.
The proof imports the existing Jacobian/abelian-variety interface for divisibility of degree-zero zero-cycles, and SF.5’s refined excess-intersection formula.

Roitman globally assumes an uncountable algebraically closed characteristic-zero field (Introduction, p. 571). Here the special-line existence argument uses only finitely many equations and the projective dimension theorem, and the curve/Jacobian divisibility argument uses surjectivity on points over any algebraically closed field. Thus this proof also covers countable algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields; no very-general-point argument is imported.
proofSteps: At x∈X choose a line whose first e−1 homogeneous intersection coefficients vanish; there are at most e−1 equations in P^{n−1}, so a nonzero direction exists. The line is contained in X or intersects it only at x with multiplicity e (Roitman Lemma 17).

Intersect this ambient line class with X using refined Gysin. In the proper-intersection case this gives e[x]; in the contained-line case the excess Chern class on the line gives the same value. All ambient line classes are rationally equivalent, so e([x]−[y])=0.

Degree-zero zero-cycles on a smooth projective connected variety over algebraically closed K are divisible: reduce to curves and use surjectivity of multiplication on their Jacobians (Roitman Proposition 1). A divisible group killed by e is zero.
A K-point exists, so degree is surjective. Smoothness, degree and the dimension inequality are preserved by algebraically closed base extension.
acceptance: e=1 gives projective space; a smooth plane conic has degree isomorphism, including e=n=2.
For a smooth plane cubic, e=3>n=2 and CH_0⁰ is nonzero; this rejects the weaker bound e≤n+1. A smooth quartic in P⁴ has e=n=4 and tests the valid boundary.
An anisotropic conic over a nonclosed field has degree image 2ℤ, so algebraic closedness cannot be removed.

sources.locator: Introduction p. 571 (uncountable-field convention); §2, Proposition 1 and Lemma 13, pp. 582–583; §5, Theorem 6(a) and Lemma 17, pp. 587–588
sources.match: Combines Jacobian divisibility with the special-line bounded-exponent argument for e≤ambient n. The displayed proof explains why this low-degree conclusion extends beyond the source’s global uncountability assumption.

nodes.title: Universal zero-dimensional support for quartic threefolds
nodes.statement: For every real closed R and every smooth quartic hypersurface X⊂P⁴_R, X is geometrically integral of dimension three and UniversalCH0Support(X,0). More explicitly, for each algebraically closed extension L/R, degree identifies CH_0(X_L) with ℤ and every L-point generates it. Hence X satisfies the surface-support hypothesis and the two rational vanishing conclusions above with d=3.
hypotheses: Smooth means the hypersurface is geometrically smooth; over the algebraic closure a smooth positive-dimensional hypersurface in P⁴ is connected and integral.
No assertion that X has an R-point, or that CH_0(X_K)→ℤ is an integral isomorphism for every nonclosed K/R, is included.
proofSteps: Base change to any algebraically closed L/R; char L=0, e=n=4, so apply low-degree-hypersurface-ch0.
Choose an L-point and its zero-dimensional reduced support. Its CH_0 pushforward is surjective by the degree computation.
Apply monotonicity from bound zero to two and then real-universal-surface-vanishing.
acceptance: The Fermat quartic x₀⁴+⋯+x₄⁴=0 over R has no R-points but satisfies this support conclusion after every algebraically closed extension.
A rational point over R is not used to choose all the witnesses; witnesses are chosen over each L.
This application is independent of the real integral Hodge conjecture for quartics, which is an MC.7 target.

nodes.title: Intermediate Euler indices
nodes.statement: For a proper finite-type k-scheme X and i≥0, define the ideal ELW_i(X)⊂ℤ generated by χ(X,F) for coherent F with support dimension at most i. Set ELW_{−1}(X)=0; set ind_i(X) to the nonnegative generator of ELW_i(X). For i≥dim X the ideals stabilize. In particular ind_0 is the ordinary index, the gcd of the degrees of closed points. Zero ideals, including the empty scheme, have generator zero. Here BW’s notation ind_i is separated from Kollár’s ideal-valued elw_i.
hypotheses: Coherent Euler characteristic is the finite alternating sum of k-dimensions for proper schemes, imported from SF.2.
The support filtration on coherent G_0 and proper pushforward belong to SchemeKTheoryOperations, not a second construction in MC.0.
No regularity or smoothness hypothesis is needed for the definition.
proofSteps: Take the image under coherent Euler characteristic of the dimension-i support filtration, then the generated ideal of ℤ.
Apply existing coherent-support dévissage: χ(F) modulo the lower-support ideal is the sum of generic lengths times χ(O_Z) on top-dimensional integral supports.
Use proper birational pushforward to replace each O_Z by the structure sheaf of its normalization modulo lower-dimensional terms. This also proves the gcd formula used in BW Proposition 3.10.
acceptance: ELW_i⊂ELW_{i+1}; hence ind_{i+1} divides ind_i, not the reverse.
The index is a gcd of degrees of arbitrary integral zero-cycles; it need not be the degree of an effective point.

nodes.title: Euler characteristic modulo the lower index
nodes.statement: For proper X/k and i≥0, send a dimension-i integral cycle α=Σ_Z n_Z[Z] to χ_i(α)=Σ_Z n_Z χ(Z,O_Z) modulo ELW_{i−1}(X), equivalently modulo ind_{i−1}(X). This factors through rational and then algebraic equivalence to a homomorphism CH_i(X)/Alg_i(X/k)→ELW_i(X)/ELW_{i−1}(X)⊂ℤ/ELW_{i−1}(X). For i=0 the lower ideal is zero and the map is ordinary degree into ℤ. Normalizing Z leaves its congruence unchanged.

The displayed sum defines χ of a formal cycle linearly; it is not χ of the structure sheaf of its union or of a nonreduced thickening.
In the target ℤ/(0)=ℤ; no division or modulus-by-a-positive-generator convention is imposed at index zero.
proofSteps: Use the cycle-to-associated-graded coherent G_0 map already owned by SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.7. Coherent dévissage and Euler characteristic send its lower-filtration ambiguity to ELW_{i−1}. This proves rational invariance.

For algebraic invariance replace an algebraically trivial cycle by an actual difference of effective flat cycle fibres over a smooth curve (ACMV Lemma 2.18, with the two projections corrected as in E51).

Apply constancy of Euler characteristic to each proper flat family. Dévissage identifies a fibre’s structure-sheaf Euler characteristic with the sum over its top components, modulo ELW_{i−1}; embedded/lower-dimensional pieces give exactly that error ideal. Thus the two cycle congruences agree.
Use proper-push Euler characteristic and the generic-degree dévissage formula to prove naturality; normalization changes the value only by lower-dimensional support.

The target image is ELW_i/ELW_{i−1}; components of dimension below i contribute nothing there.

nodes.title: A homologically trivial cycle detected by Euler parity
nodes.statement: Let F=ℂ((t))((u))((v)) and let X⊂P⁴_F be the smooth anisotropic quadric of q=⟨1,t,u,tu,v⟩. Then dim X=3, ind_0(X)=2, and CH_1(X) has a torsion subgroup ℤ/2 with generator τ whose χ_1 value is 1 modulo 2. The integral arithmetic group H⁴_et(X,ℤ₂(2)) is torsion-free, so the integral arithmetic cycle class of τ is zero. Consequently τ is homologically trivial for this map but not algebraically trivial over F. Tensoring CH_1 with ℚ kills τ, so this does not contradict the classical rational comparison chain.
hypotheses: Characteristic is zero and the étale group is arithmetic over F, not the group after algebraic closure and not a selected classical Weil theory.

The complete Clifford/K_0 calculation of χ_1(τ) and the integral Hochschild–Serre calculation are verification obligations MC0-G2 and MC0-G3, rather than assumptions silently absorbed into a cycle-class API.
proofSteps: Successive Laurent valuations prove anisotropy: ⟨1,t⟩ over ℂ((t)), then its twofold Pfister product ⟨1,t,u,tu⟩ over ℂ((t))((u)), and finally its sum with v⟨1⟩. Springer’s odd-degree anisotropy theorem makes all closed-point degrees even; adjoining √(−v) gives a degree-two point. Thus ind_0=2.
Since −1 is a square, the first four coefficients form a twofold Pfister form. Karpenko Theorem 5.3 gives TCH²(X)=ℤ/2; for the threefold CH²=CH_1.

Use the topological filtration on integral K_0, the CH²≃gr²_top K_0 comparison (§3.1), and the Clifford-index lattice of §3.3–3.8. Identify the torsion lift with the integral class whose split representative is ℓ₀=[O_point] and hence has χ=1. The explicit index/lift computation is MC0-G2.

Calculate H⁴_et(X,ℤ₂(2)) by integral Hochschild–Serre over F, including its filtration, differentials and extensions, to establish torsion-freeness (MC0-G3). A rational spectral sequence does not establish this.
A homomorphism from the order-two τ to a torsion-free target is zero; the Euler congruence is nonzero and factors through algebraic equivalence, proving the non-equivalence.
acceptance: Preserve all three Laurent parameters and the fifth coefficient v; replacing F by ℂ destroys the example.
The nonzero Euler parity distinguishes τ from zero even though its arithmetic integral cycle class and rational Chow class are zero.
Torsion-free geometric H⁴ alone is insufficient: arithmetic Hochschild–Serre contributions must be checked.

Present the continuation as three ordered interfaces: correspondence algebra; adequate and algebraic quotient comparisons; integral support/cohomology-sheaf and Euler-index applications. SF.2/SF.4/SF.5 and SchemeKTheoryOperations own the general supplier extensions, as recorded in MC0-R1–R8. No new atlas planet is added beyond the existing six.
restructure.reason: Keeps integral counterexamples distinct from rational motives and avoids duplicating intersection, K-theory, Picard and cohomology foundations.

sourceIssues.reason: The rank is N+1−g, so the free projective-bundle basis ends at rank minus one. Dimension counting gives dim W_j+(N−g)−j=i+N. sourceIssues.locator: Remark 2.5, assertion about every degree-N zero-cycle and its proof, printed p. 12 (PDF p. 36) of Astérisque 455 (2025); coefficient rings as in Definition 2.1 p. 11.
sourceIssues.printed: For a strict R-decomposition of NΔ, the remark identifies Z₂ with the pullback of any degree-N zero-cycle and claims all such cycles are rationally equivalent to its chosen α, without a hypothesis excluding N-torsion.
sourceIssues.correction: The action argument gives Nβ=deg(β)α, hence N(β−α)=0 when deg β=deg α=N. Keep this bounded-exponent conclusion; uniqueness requires additional N-torsion-freeness (or that N be invertible). The special N=1 conclusion with a rational point is valid. MC.0 uses only annihilation and then rationalization.
sourceIssues.reason: Cancellation of N in CH_0 is not valid generally. A counterexample within the stated arbitrary-ring scope is R=ℤ/2, N=2, and X=E_K for an elliptic curve E/ℂ and K=ℂ(E). Then 2Δ=0 admits the zero strict decomposition. The degree-two integral cycle β=2[O]+([η]−[O]) has nonzero image in CH_0(X)⊗ℤ/2: η is not twice a K-point, since that would extend to a rational map φ:E→E with [2]∘φ=id, contradicting degrees 4·deg φ=1. Thus the pullback pr₂^*β is nonzero (restrict to {O}×X), although Z₂=0. The display only forces 2β=0 in these coefficients. This finding concerns the general coefficient assertion, not the N=1 universal-triviality equivalence.

review.reason: Confirmed for the stated arbitrary coefficient rings. The action equation implies only N-torsion of the difference of degree-N classes. In the recorded F₂, N=2 elliptic example, a half of the generic point would give a rational self-map with 4·deg φ=1, so the degree-two class has nonzero mod-two image despite the zero strict decomposition. This refutes the arbitrary-ring uniqueness claim, without affecting the N=1 consequence.
